title: Implementer presets allow moving and removing files (with S440)

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Observed 2026-11-11 (slicer s453, ork-20261111-213809-376f): the implementer under `ork projects set slicer --preset python` was denied `git -C <worktree> ls-files -s tests/fixtures/relay-contract-v11.json` and `git mv tests/fixtures/relay-contract-v11.json tests/fixtures/relay-contract-v12.json` while doing the slice's own fixture rename; the run went on. Wanted: decide whether the presets allow `git ls-files` (read-only) and `git mv` (index-only, no commit), or say in the brief that a rename is a plain move the landing picks up.

Evidence (2026-11-18):

- Both presets share one head and tail (`internal/engine/perm.go:45-69`): git `status`, `diff` and `log`, plain and `-C *`, and no `ls-files`, `mv` or `rm`. The built-in default is the go preset (`internal/engine/perm.go:75-78`, adj 75 and adj 94).
- A plain move needs `mv` or `rm`, and neither is in either list, so the implementer today can only Write the new file and leave the old one. ork's commit stages everything (`git add -A`, `internal/engine/states.go:1284`), so a rename done by the implementer by any means is picked up at the commit.
- A preset is written into the registry as a plain list when it is set (`internal/daemon/settings.go:114-120`; `docs/state.md:161`). Changing `ImplementerPreset` changes the built-in default and later `--preset` calls, not a project that already stores a list (slicer does).
- S440 (filed from tool feedback, adj 466 decided `file`) asks for `rm` or `git rm` for the same reason: a file the slice moves out of. S440 and this slice change the same lines (`internal/engine/perm.go:45-69`).
- adj 457 (`launch.allowlist-rg`) dropped `rg` from the presets because `rg --pre` runs a program; the same review applies to any new entry.

Open owner question: which move and index-read forms the presets allow, per the owner's answer to `launch.allowlist-move`.

sections.body:

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Owner decision adj 478 (`launch.allowlist-move` = all, 2026-11-18): the go and python presets and the built-in default allow `git ls-files` and `git mv` (plain and `-C *`), `git rm` (plain and `-C *`), and plain `rm` without a recursive flag. S440 (file removal) is merged into this slice.

- `TestImplementerPresetsAllowGitLsFilesAndMv` in `internal/engine/perm_test.go`: for both `go` and `python`, the list holds `Bash(git ls-files*)`, `Bash(git -C * ls-files*)`, `Bash(git mv*)` and `Bash(git -C * mv*)`. Red today: none is in either list (`internal/engine/perm.go:46-53`).
- `TestImplementerPresetsAllowFileRemoval` in `internal/engine/perm_test.go`: both presets contain `Bash(git rm *)`, `Bash(git -C * rm *)` and `Bash(rm *)`. Red today.
- `TestDefaultImplementerAllowlistIsExactlyTheDecidedOne` in `internal/engine/perm_test.go`: update its exact list to the new base. Red today against the new expected list.
- `TestApprovalAllowsRemovingAFileInTheWorktree` in `internal/agent/claude/pretool_test.go`: with the new allowlist, `git rm cmd/ork/start_unix.go` and `rm tests/x.py.tail` from the worktree are allowed. Red today: no allowlist entry matches.
- `TestApprovalDeniesRemovingOutsideTheWorktree` in `internal/agent/claude/pretool_test.go`: `rm ../other/file`, `rm /home/x/file` and `git -C /elsewhere rm f` are denied with "outside worktree". Green today on the path rule; it guards the new entries.
- `TestApprovalDeniesRecursiveRemove` in `internal/agent/claude/pretool_test.go`: `rm -r dir`, `rm -rf .`, `rm -fr x` and `rm --recursive x` are not allowed by the new entry. Red today once the plain `Bash(rm *)` entry exists; the hook guard makes it green.
- `TestImplementerPromptSaysHowToRename` in `internal/roles/roles_test.go`: the implementer prompt names `git mv` for a rename of a tracked file, and says a file the slice moves code out of, or created by mistake, is removed rather than left as a stub. Red today.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests and see each red for the stated reason.
2. `ImplementerPreset`: add the adj 478 entries to the shared base, so both presets and the built-in default get them. Keep the order stable; the check command's entry stays last. A part role keeps them (they are not slicer writes, `internal/engine/perm.go:81-100`).
3. Approval hook: refuse a recursive flag (`-r`, `-R`, `-rf`, `-fr`, `--recursive`) for the plain rm entry, so a match on `Bash(rm *)` alone never allows a tree removal. Vet git mv's options the way adj 457 did for rg.
4. Implementer prompt: one line that a tracked file is renamed with `git mv` and ork's commit picks up the move; one line that a file the slice moves code out of, or created by mistake, is removed with `git rm` or `rm`, not left as a stub.
5. A project that stores a list keeps it: the docs say to run `ork projects set NAME --preset go|python` again, or `--allow implementer=PATTERN` (adj 190, adds), to pick up the new entries. ork does not rewrite stored lists.
6. Docs: `docs/design.md` preset lists (cite adj 478 next to adj 75 and adj 94), `docs/state.md:161`, `docs/guide.md:255`. Changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S345 --text "..."`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- The go and python presets, and the built-in default, allow git ls-files, git mv, git rm and non-recursive rm (adj 478).
- A removal outside the worktree is denied; a recursive rm is not allowed by the new entry.
- The S350 case (an untracked stray file) and the S431 case (a tracked file the slice moved out of) both have an allowed form.
- The implementer prompt says how to rename and how to remove a file.
- The docs list the new entries, cite adj 478, and say how a project with a stored list picks them up.

Commands:
- `go test ./internal/engine ./internal/agent/claude ./internal/roles -run 'TestImplementerPreset|TestDefaultImplementerAllowlist|TestApprovalAllowsRemoving|TestApprovalDeniesRemoving|TestApprovalDeniesRecursive|TestImplementerPromptSaysHowToRename' -v`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` exits 0.
- `adj lint` exits 0.
